authors: Galvagnion C, Buell AK, Meisl G, et al.
title: Lipid vesicles trigger alpha-synuclein aggregation by stimulating primary nucleation
notes: DMPS-only mechanistic study (DMPS is NOT one of the 8 candidates). Important conceptual evidence: the SAME lipid is biphasic - excess lipid (ratio>40) gives NO aggregation and even DISSOLVES preformed fibrils, while low ratio accelerates (max rate ~ratio 8). Supports 'formulation/ratio changes direction'.

authors: Gaspar R, Pallbo J, Weininger U, Linse S, Sparr E
title: Ganglioside lipids accelerate alpha-synuclein amyloid formation
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta - Proteins and Proteomics
notes: Lipid-induced paradigm at pH 5.5. Candidate-relevant: DOPC (no aggregation), GM1 (acceleration). Explicitly notes GM1 vesicles INHIBIT at neutral pH (ref 67), i.e. opposite direction - the key condition-dependence for GM1.

authors: Matveyenka M, Ali A, Mitchell CL, Brown HC, Kurouski D
title: Cholesterol Accelerates Aggregation of alpha-Synuclein Simultaneously Increasing the Toxicity of Amyloid Fibrils
notes: AGGREGATING-BASELINE paradigm: 40 uM alpha-syn in PBS pH 7.4, 37 C, 510 rpm SHAKING, 1:1 lipid:protein, LUVs, 2 mM ThT - protein aggregates alone (t1/2~82 h) and lipids modulate. FIRST paper here with explicit numeric t_lag and t1/2. Directly tests CHOLESTEROL and DPPC (both candidates). Key results: pure DPPC and 60% cholesterol ACCELERATE (shorten lag/t1/2); 15-30% cholesterol no effect. Cites Dou et al. that DMPC strongly SUPPRESSES but DPPC does not (a 14->16 carbon change flips the effect). NOTE: this CONTRADICTS a naive 'ordered lipids are protective' expectation - see docs/chemistry_rules.md Rule 8 revision.
